a:r.a:t: Hi everyone, my project is called "U.S. Retail Gasoline Price Forecast."

The goal is to build a full stack data science application, not just a model in a notebook. The app collects weekly U.S. gasoline price data from the EIA, turns that time series into model features, trains two forecasting models, and then serves predictions through a Flask API. A separate Streamlit dashboard calls that API so users can choose the forecasting method and forecast horizon interactively.

The current dataset has 1,729 weekly observations from 1993 through May 18, 2026. I serve two models, XGBoost and SARIMA, and the final project is deployed as two live services: one Cloud Run service for the Flask model API and another Cloud Run service for the Streamlit interface.

The important idea on this slide is that the project follows the production-style requirement from class: the app and the model API are hosted separately, and the user interface communicates with the model through an API call.
